claim: For a pair of tetrahedrally lobed patchy particles in the fully staggered, touching configuration at compression ratio 0.7, Monte Carlo integration of the excluded-volume overlap shows the separate lobe-lobe overlap regions stay separate for depletant-to-lobe radius ratios up to 0.075 but overlap from 0.10 upward, where adding up pairwise depletion potentials overestimates the attraction by up to 30%; pairwise depletion potentials therefore fail for large depletants on these shapes.

numbers.name: depletant_to_colloid_radius_ratio
numbers.note: largest ratio at which the overlap regions stay separate.

numbers.name: depletant_to_colloid_radius_ratio
numbers.note: ratio from which they overlap and pairwise additivity overestimates.

validity_conditions: A GEOMETRIC CALCULATION, not a dynamics result: Monte Carlo integration of the depletant-excluded volume for a fixed pair, compared with the sum of pairwise overlaps, for depletant-to-lobe radius ratios from 0.01 to 0.20 at compression ratio 0.7. It warns against the pairwise-additive depletion potential common in molecular dynamics, including the kind this paper's own dynamics uses; the paper's own runs sit at a ratio of 0.02, below the 0.075 up to which the overlap regions stay separate.
